candidates.changed_node: top-level MUL joining A's (operating_margin*asset_turnover) with B's (roe*book_per_share), under one new outer CS_RANK
candidates.rationale: A donates its DuPont efficiency numerator ($operating_margin*$asset_turnover, 3 nodes); B donates its equity-profitability numerator ($roe*$book_per_share, 3 nodes). Both parents' own leverage/range normalizers are dropped rather than reused, since either verbatim ratio restates its parent's archived block. The two raw products are multiplied first and ranked only once at the top -- bare-ranking either fragment alone would restate a third archive member (RANK(om*at) is live in 2e7fb35702283a1d, RANK(roe*bps) is live in 6c40493b8287c013). Fusion logic: a capital-efficiency/equity-profitability CONFIRMATION signal -- rewards names strong on both DuPont axes at once, something neither single ratio (each distortable by one accounting lever) can express alone.

candidates.changed_node: top-level MUL joining (roe*book_per_share) with a re-windowed TS_CORR(volume, high-low, 21), under one new CS_RANK
candidates.rationale: A donates $roe*$book_per_share (3 nodes, its quality numerator). B donates $high-$low (3 nodes) rewired into a fresh TS_CORR($volume, ., 21) -- window moved from B's own 10 so the 6-node correlation block isn't a verbatim restatement of B. B's own admitted rationale reads volume/range co-movement as informed-trading intensity. Fusion logic: multiplying quality by that intensity asks whether a quality name's price action is currently backed by genuine informed volume rather than noise -- a confirmation neither parent alone expresses (A has no volume information; B has no fundamental content).

candidates.changed_node: top-level MUL joining a re-windowed TS_CORR(volume, high-low, 15) with a new TS_RANK(DELAY(close,21) - close, 21) term
candidates.rationale: A donates $high-$low (3 nodes) inside a re-windowed correlation (15, not A's own 10, to avoid restating A's 6-node block). B donates DELAY($close, 21) (3 nodes) -- the deliberately stale reference B's own lineage says was pushed out specifically to decorrelate from short lags. Fusion logic: a month-old-reference price move (B's idea), time-series-ranked, multiplied by whether volume is currently confirming the day's range (A's informed-trading proxy) -- trusts a stale-reference momentum move more when concurrent volume/range co-movement says real information is arriving. Neither parent alone carries both a directional reference and an information-flow measure.

candidates.changed_node: new top-level MUL joining B's (close - high) fade with a fresh (open - DELAY(close,21)) monthly-gap term
candidates.rationale: A donates DELAY($close, 21) (3 nodes), its deliberately stale reference point. B donates $close-$high (3 nodes), its same-day fade-from-high term; both parents' own guards/wrappers (A's TS_MEAN+division-by-delayed-close, B's TS_RANK+CS_RANK scaffolding) are dropped since reusing either whole would restate the parent verbatim. Fusion logic: conditions the same-day high-fade on a fresh open-vs-month-ago-close gap -- a fade means something different in a name that has already re-rated substantially over the last month (exhaustion) versus one sitting flat. Neither parent alone combines same-day positioning with a monthly reference level.

candidates.changed_node: new MUL of A's (close-low) recovery wick with B's (close-high) fade wick, guarded by dollar_volume
candidates.rationale: A donates $close-$low (3 nodes, its own-admitted 'support recovery' wick) and the idea of a dollar_volume scale (guard reused only as a fresh divisor, not A's literal ratio, which would restate A's 7-node block). B donates $close-$high (3 nodes, its fade wick). Fusion logic: the product of the two wicks is zero when close pins either extreme and most negative when close sits mid-range on a wide bar -- a joint 'how one-sided was today's close' measure, liquidity-scaled so a small illiquid name's swing counts less than a mega-cap's. Neither parent alone sees both wicks together; each only sees its own side of the day's range.

candidates.changed_node: top-level MUL joining B's (roe*book_per_share) with A's (close-high), under one new CS_RANK
candidates.rationale: A donates $close-$high (3 nodes, same-day fade from the high). B donates $roe*$book_per_share (3 nodes, its quality numerator); B's own range normalizer is dropped rather than reused. The raw product is ranked once at the top rather than ranking either fragment alone, which would restate A itself or the archived RANK(roe*bps) in 6c40493b8287c013. Fusion logic: quality-conditioned reversal -- a fade from the day's high in a high-ROE, high-book-value name reads as a dip worth buying (support expected), while the same fade in a low-quality name does not. A has no fundamental content; B has no same-day positional information.

candidates.changed_node: new MUL of (roe*book_per_share) with earnings_per_share, divided by B's own (close+1e-8) guard, ranked once
candidates.rationale: A donates $roe*$book_per_share (3 nodes). B donates its ($close + 1e-8) price guard (3 nodes) plus the earnings-yield concept via the bare $earnings_per_share field -- B's literal EPS/(close+eps) ratio is not reused as a block, since that would restate B's own 5-node core computation. Fusion logic: multiplying EPS by the quality block before dividing by price is a quality-weighted earnings yield ('quality at a reasonable price') -- cheap names are only rewarded when ROE and book value per share also confirm quality, closing the value-trap gap in B's raw EPS/price signal. A has no valuation anchor; B has no quality dimension.

candidates.changed_node: new SUB of earnings_per_share and B's TS_DELTA(book_per_share, 63), scaled by A's (close+1e-8) guard
candidates.rationale: A donates its ($close + 1e-8) price guard (3 nodes); its literal EPS/(close+eps) ratio is not reused since that restates A's own 5-node block, so bare $earnings_per_share carries A's valuation content instead. B donates TS_DELTA($book_per_share, 63) (3 nodes), one-quarter book-value growth -- 63 days matches the only window this fundamental clears coverage at. Fusion logic: subtracting the dollar amount of recent book-value growth from current EPS, then scaling by price, asks whether earnings power is keeping pace with balance-sheet growth per dollar of price -- flags dilution/quality-erosion when book value grows faster than earnings. Neither parent alone links the earnings level to the rate of equity growth.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes
from EACH parent, checked mechanically; a child that is really just one parent
with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

In the rationale, state the fusion logic: what does the combination capture that
neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
so in the rationale rather than force it.
